Jaspreet P.: Heads-up: I'm consolidating a tiny runbook for Dedicated Capacity provisioning so new engs can get a working instance in ~10 mins. Plan: Quickstart (terraform + python), Troubleshooting (quota, preemption), and FAQ (SLA language + isolation). Any objections?
Theo M.: Sounds good. Please highlight the quota check step prominently 1st failure mode we see in onboarding.
Jaspreet P.: Will do. Draft Terraform snippet (keeps var names consistent with infra):
```terraform
data "redwood_quota" "current" {}
resource "redwood_dedicated_capacity" "quickstart" {
  name                    = "dev-quickstart"
  gpu_type                = "t4"
  reserved_pool_replicas  = 2
  scale_policy            = "autoscale"
  isolation               = "tenant"
}
```
Kira B.: For Troubleshooting: add a short bullet about eviction behavior when isolation=tenant vs reserved-pool and link to Deep Dive. Keep wording neutral.
docs-bot: link-check: broken anchor detected in handbook/dedicated/faq.md -> '#sla-details' not found.
Jaspreet P.: Thanks. I'll point SLA links to /handbook/dedicated/sla-and-slos and add a TODO to revisit anchors.
eng-runtime: Quick note: the autoscale cooldown default is 300s on the runtime side; recommend showing that explicitly in examples.
Jaspreet P.: Adding cooldown example to Python snippet and a short line on expected preemption semantics. Will open draft PR and tag #eng-runtime + #docs-review.
Theo M.: Also add a short rollback checklist: drain traffic, reduce replicas to 0, roll back infra change, re-enable traffic. Simple, actionable.
Jaspreet P.: Done. Draft PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/9922 (draft). I'll ping reviewers.
